text:
maria: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting sudden p95/p99 regression on /v1/generate starting ~09:40 PST. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s, p99 to 6-8s. Some requests are getting 429s and others are sitting in QUEUED for >5s. Seeing reports from EU and us-west. I have a repro from one customer below.

incident-bot: ALERT: route:/v1/generate p95 > 1s for 10m (grafana/dashboard/alerts/route-gen)

aj: looking. link to uptime/grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/inference-overview?orgId=1&from=now-30m - can you paste the customer repro and any request ids?

maria: repro from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-001","input":"summarize: ...","timeout_ms":60000}'
```
They see successful response sometimes but often request is queued then slow. Request id examples: req_20260315_7a9b, req_20260315_7aaf.

sam: I'm seeing admission controller log spikes starting 09:41:12. Key observations from infra metrics:
- queue_depth (route=/v1/generate, cluster=inference-prod): ~220 at peak
- active_workers: 8, concurrency_per_worker: 64 -> effective concurrency 512 (we're maxing out)
- drop/admit_reject rate (admissionctl): ~18% rejected (mostly non-priority)
- CPU on some workers hitting 98%, GPU mem stable but exec latency up (context switch + KV cache misses)
Logs (excerpt):
```
[09:41:13] admissionctl: queue_len=218, inflight=512, max_inflight=512, reject_count=42
[09:41:14] worker-5: exec_ms=1200 p95=950 p99=4500 queued_ms=320
```
So looks like overloaded workers + big queue leading to increased tail latency. Possibly a sudden traffic mix change (more long-context or embedding-heavy requests) increased token time.

aj: Any recent config changes or rollout? I don't see any deploys in the last hour. Could be traffic spike (customer batch jobs). Can we identify top callers?

sam: Top callers by token volume last 30m: account:acct-998, acct-203, some spikes from internal load-testing svc (svc-loadtest). acct-998 is a paying customer who started large batch jobs at 09:39.

kyle: I'm going to spin up +4 workers in the pool and increase autoscaler aggressiveness for the short term. Command: `rctl pool scale inference-prod +4 --reason "latency surge 2026-03-15"`

sam: Two quick mitigations we can do now (low-risk):
1) Adjust admission controller policy to favor low-latency interactive traffic and shed batch requests: set `admission_policy=prefer_interactive` and `max_queue=100`.
2) Enable fallback routing to `rwd-medium-001` for non-critical requests (reduces per-token cost & exec time).
Commands I'm proposing:
```
admitctl update-policy --route /v1/generate --policy prefer_interactive --max-queue 100
router update-route --route /v1/generate --fallback-model rwd-medium-001 --priority-only false
```
I can roll these in 2-3 min.

maria: customer acct-998 confirms they launched a large multi-threaded batch around 09:39, they didn't expect it to affect interactive traffic. They're ok with temporarily throttling their jobs if we ask.

harpreet: support_lead: Offer them a staggered window and apply quota reduction for batch traffic while we stabilize. Also prepare a brief incident note for customers.

nina: I can confirm switching to the medium model reduces p95 locally to ~220ms for our test requests — but quality difference is notable for some prompts. We'll need to offer it as an explicit opt-in or automatic fallback only for low-priority requests.

aj: Good. Two things: (A) Sam/Kyle, apply the admission change + scale now. (B) Maria, ask acct-998 to pause their batch for 30m while we stabilize. I'll open an incident ticket and start a short postmortem tracker.

kyle: scaled +4 workers, new total active_workers=12. Autoscale cooldown reduced to 30s for emergency.

sam: admission policy updated and fallback enabled. Command logs:
```
> admitctl update-policy ... ok
> router update-route ... ok
```
Monitoring shows queue depth dropping from 220 -> 48 over 4 minutes. p95 trending down to ~180ms.

maria: contacted acct-998; they paused their run. Customer confirms latency improving in their environment.

aj: Nice work. Remaining tasks:
- keep autoscale up until traffic normalizes (Kyle)
- root cause: why did acct-998's batch impact interactive routing so hard? Was isolation broken? (Sam/AJ)
- evaluate admissionctl defaults so a single customer can't push interactive p99 so high (Product/Runtime)
- follow-up with acct-998 to discuss dedicated capacity/reserved pool options

harpreet: I'll draft the customer communication and send your notes. Please paste the exact commands and timings into the incident doc.

sam: quick note: we saw a secondary issue where KV cache misses were amplified after the scaling event; investigating a cache-warm strategy for new workers.

maria: summary for incident doc: started 09:40 PST, impacted interactive p95/p99 across regions, root trigger: large parallel batch from acct-998 causing queueing; mitigations: scaled +4 workers, admission policy change (prefer_interactive, max_queue=100), enabled fallback to rwd-medium-001, asked customer to pause; result: queue depth back to ~40 and p95 ~180ms. Next steps: postmortem and quota/dedicated capacity recommendation.

aj: I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up sync in 1 hour to decide long-term mitigations. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: closing thread for now — will update incident doc with timestamps and commands. If anything regresses ping @aj or @sam.
